nodes.name: Corruption
nodes.summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era onward (Beast, Vaal, Eternal Empire)

sources.locator: intro: 'The Beast possesses corrupting powers, devouring the souls of his prey and mutating whoever comes in contact with it.'
section '==Kitava==' > Dialogue, Haku's 'Kaom' option: 'Kitava, God of Corruption, consumed Kaom from heart to skin.'
section '===Precursor civilization===': 'After mastering corruption, they delved deeper...'; the Precursor Weapon is one 'which Doryani attempts to harness to destroy corruption'

nodes.name: Cataclysm
nodes.summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)

sources.locator: intro: 'An incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.'; section '====The Vaal Cataclysm====': 'The Vaal Cataclysm, also known as The Fall, was a historical event...'
section '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===': 'The Cataclysm brought an end to Voll's reign and the Eternal Empire as a whole.'
page intro: 'Cataclysm's Wake is an epilogue quest. It act as the tutorial quest for the Atlas.'

nodes.name: Eternal Empire (era)
nodes.summary: Umbrella period of the Eternal Empire (Sarn Empire) from Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC) through the Reign of Voll to the Cataclysm (~1339 IC). Split into the era_eternal_empire_rise and era_eternal_empire_fall buckets; the faction itself is faction_eternal_empire.

nodes.name: PoE1 (era umbrella)

nodes.name: PoE2 (era umbrella)

nodes.name: Kastov
nodes.summary: Governor of Stridevolf in the Eternal Empire who joined High Templar Voll's Purity Rebellion in 1333 IC against the gemling thaumatocracy. Per the Victario page, unlike Voll, Ondar, Geofri and Adus he did not turn undead or into a ghost in the in-game present.

sources.locator: intro paragraph: 'Governor Kastov of Stridevolf' listed among Voll's allies with Lord Mayor Ondar, Victario, Archbishop Geofri and Commander Adus

paragraph 'In 1333 IC, Victario supported the Purity Rebellion ... along with Kastov, Lord Mayor Ondar, Archbishop Geofri and Commander Adus'; and 'neither Victario nor Kastov turned into the undead or a ghost'
section '==Members==' > Purity Rebellion rebels: '** [[Kastov]], Governor of [[Stridevolf]]'
section 'Notable members': 'Governor Kastov of Stridevolf'

nodes.name: Letters of Exile
nodes.summary: Environmental lore object in Lioneye's Watch: court papers nailed to stakes that give the sentences of named exiles (1597-1599 IC) in the formula 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. Added in version 0.10.8. Distinct from text_letters_from_chitus (Chitus's letters to Cadiro) and text_vaal_letters (Vaal victims' letters).

sources.locator: intro: 'Letters of Exile is an environmental lore object found in Lioneye's Watch.'; section '==Format==' sentencing formula; version history 0.10.8

nodes.name: Kamasa's Orb of Sacrifice
nodes.summary: PoE2 currency orb (introduced 0.5.4) that removes a random explicit modifier to upgrade a Corruption enchantment on a Rare Amulet, Ring or Belt. Drops from the Royal Trove in Atziri's Temple after defeating Atziri, the Red Queen. Its name matches the deity deity_kamasa; the item page does not state a naming origin.

sources.locator: title and description: 'Kamasa's Orb of Sacrifice' - 'Upgrades a Corruption Enchantment on a Rare Amulet, Ring or Belt and removes a Random Modifier'; drop_text: 'Can drop from Royal Trove in Atziri's Temple after defeating Atziri, the Red Queen.'

nodes.name: Citaqualotl's Thesis
nodes.summary: PoE2 Ancient Soul Core (introduced 0.4.0 with Fate of the Vaal). Its socket effects for Body Armour, Gloves and Boots concern Offerings, Sacrifice and Guard. Flavour text frames it as research into altering reality: 'Let us start not with ourselves, but with willing subjects.'

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'Altering reality, even locally, is no simple matter. Let us start not with ourselves, but with willing subjects.'; version history 0.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

nodes.name: Guatelitzi's Thesis
nodes.summary: PoE2 Ancient Soul Core (introduced 0.4.0 with Fate of the Vaal). Helmet, Body Armour and Boots effects concern Life lost from hits, Recoup and Sprinting. Flavour text: 'We are nothing but flesh. Blood. If we are to ascend, we must empower that flesh.'

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'We are nothing but flesh. Blood. If we are to ascend, we must empower that flesh.'; version history 0.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

nodes.name: Jiquani's Thesis
nodes.summary: PoE2 Ancient Soul Core (introduced 0.4.0 with Fate of the Vaal). Helmet, Gloves and Boots effects concern maximum Mana, Energy Shield recharge and movement speed. Flavour text: 'The soul carries the truth of what we are. That is where we should focus our efforts.'

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'The soul carries the truth of what we are. That is where we should focus our efforts.'; version history 0.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

nodes.name: Quipolatl's Thesis
nodes.summary: PoE2 Ancient Soul Core (introduced 0.4.0 with Fate of the Vaal). Flavour text presents the research as altering the fundamental laws of existence through focused Corruption: 'With enough focused Corruption, we can alter the fundamental laws of existence in a small area'.

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'The results prove it. With enough focused Corruption, we can alter the fundamental laws of existence in a small area... the question now: what do we try first?'; version history 0.4.0 'Introduced to the game.'

nodes.name: Guatelitzi's Ablation
nodes.summary: PoE2 lineage support gem (introduced 0.4.0) for Offering skills: supported skills Sacrifice 25% of Life on use, and the Offerings they create grant Power Charges. Drops from the Lineage Gems Vault (Hall of Reverence) in Atziri's Temple. Its flavour text describes young Guatelitzi preparing prisoners for sacrifice.

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'Young Guatelitzi was found moving among the prisoners, preparing their living bodies for sacrifice. The High Priests recognised his inclinations, and gave him a higher calling.'; drop_text: 'Drops from a Lineage Gems Vault (Hall of Reverence) in Atziri's Temple.'; version history 0.4.0

nodes.name: Hayoxi's Fulmination
nodes.summary: PoE2 lineage support gem (introduced 0.4.0) for Curse skills: supported Curses create cursed ground that, after 7 seconds of persistence, triggers the Annihilation column. Drops from the Lineage Gems Vault (Hall of Reverence) in Atziri's Temple. Flavour text names an 'Architect of Destruction' who laid explosive powder under the royal temple.

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'The Architect of Destruction slipped explosive powder under the royal temple one pinch at a time.'; drop_text: 'Drops from a Lineage Gems Vault (Hall of Reverence) in Atziri's Temple.'; version history 0.4.0

nodes.name: Guatelitzi
nodes.summary: Figure known only from the flavour text of Guatelitzi's Ablation (drop location Atziri's Temple): as a young man he was found among prisoners 'preparing their living bodies for sacrifice', and the High Priests recognised his inclinations and gave him a higher calling. Vaal placement is inferred from the Atziri's Temple drop location, not stated.

chronology.relative: Vaal era (inferred from Atziri's Temple drop location; no date stated)

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'Young Guatelitzi was found moving among the prisoners, preparing their living bodies for sacrifice. The High Priests recognised his inclinations, and gave him a higher calling.'

nodes.name: Hayoxi
nodes.summary: Figure called 'The Architect of Destruction' in the flavour text of Hayoxi's Fulmination, who laid explosive powder under the royal temple 'one pinch at a time' and never found the courage to light it. Identity beyond the flavour text is not recorded in the corpus. Placement in the Vaal era is inferred from the royal-temple setting.

chronology.relative: Vaal era (inferred from royal-temple setting; no date stated)

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'The Architect of Destruction slipped explosive powder under the royal temple one pinch at a time. For years, he clung to that, never finding the courage to light it.'
